en: The Apadāna of the Elder Saccasaññaka Hatthivagga 3.3 [Verse 1] When the Teacher, the Buddha, the Fully Enlightened One, was dwelling at Rājagaha, the city of Giribbaja, I was then a young elephant, seven years of age. [Verse 2] I saw the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Fully Enlightened One, seated upon a stone slab, surrounded by a great assembly of monks. [Verse 3] Having seen him, my mind became joyful; I approached the Teacher and spoke these words: "O Great Hero, O Great Sage, please teach me the Truth. [Verse 4] Then the Teacher, the Buddha, the Fully Enlightened One, knowing my intention, taught me the Truth in brief, beginning with the words: "All conditioned things are impermanent. [Verse 5] Having heard that teaching, I attained the fruit of Stream-entry. Then, having paid homage to the Teacher, I departed from his presence. [Verse 6] After passing away from that state, I was reborn in the world of the gods. Having enjoyed celestial pleasures for a long time, I was reborn here in the human realm. [Verse 7] In this very life, I have realized the fruit of Arhatship. Through the power of that truth, I am now known as Saccasaññaka. [Verse 8] By means of this truth, may I never fall into the lower realms. May I always be born among humans and devas, and eventually attain Parinibbāna. [Verse 9] Through this truthful declaration, may all my aspirations be fulfilled. May I never be separated from the Buddhas, and may I quickly attain the supreme state of Buddhahood.
At that time, Vessabhū,
seated at the head of the community of monks,
taught the Noble Truths.
Extinguishing the great multitude,
having attained supreme compassion,
I went to the assembly.
While sitting there,
I listened to the Dhamma from the Teacher;
having heard that Dhamma from him, I—
I went to the world of the gods;
for thirty eons, I dwelt there among the devas in the past.
In the thirty-first aeon from now,
whatever perception I attained then,
I do not know any state of woe.
This is the fruit of the perception of truth.
Twenty-six aeons ago,
I was once a lord of men.
By the name Ekaphusita,
he was a Cakkavatti of great power.
The four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā)...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Saccasaññaka speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Saccasaññaka is the third.
